Travis County ESD No. 4.canvasser: the Travis County ESD No. 4 board of emergency services commissioners
Travis County ESD No. 4.canvass_cite: Election Code §67.002 (governing body canvasses) default; the ESD 4 order (an SOS form, partly scanned) has no canvass section https://votetravis.gov/wp-content/uploads/TC-ESD-4_Order-the-Election-8-14-26.pdf
Travis County ESD No. 4.counties_cite: Order and notice: 'Confirming the Expansion of District Territory of Travis County Emergency Service District 4'; notice addressed to registered voters of Travis County https://votetravis.gov/wp-content/uploads/TCESD4_Notice-of-Election_UPDATED.pdf
Travis County ESD No. 4.notes: One proposition (c205): add about 140 properties on the east shore of the Colorado River (Lake Austin) between Pennybacker Bridge and Emma Long Park that were disannexed from the City of Austin, with the territory assuming its share of debts and taxes. ESD 4 site 'DisAnnexation and Joining ESD 4' https://www.esd4.org/disannexation-and-joining-esd-4: property owners in the disannexed area collected petition signatures (May 30, 2026), submitted the petition to ESD 4 with 'over 80 signatures' (July 1), ESD 4 verified it and ordered a hearing (July 14), the formal hearing was held Aug 14, and the election was ordered Aug 14. That is the H&S Code §775.051 petition-annexation procedure (petition by qualified voters owning property in the territory, then hearing, then board approval by resolution). §775.051(f): annexation needs 'a majority of the voters at an election held in the district' and 'a majority of the voters at a separate election held in the territory to be annexed' (https://texas.public.law/statutes/tex._health_and_safety_code_section_775.051). §§775.052-.053 cover dissolution, not annexation. By statute, then, BOTH the existing district and the territory vote, in separate elections, and each needs its own majority. However, the county ballot lists ESD 4 only once, with a single proposition. Unlike ESD 9 and ESD 10, there is no split into district and territory versions. The ESD 4 order (a scanned SOS form) and its notice do not say who votes or whether the two electorates are tallied separately. Its single combined proposition also departs from §775.051(g), which provides two ballot forms. ESD 4's handout (https://www.esd4.org/files/2b5c7fa56/Expansion+Election+Public+Information+handout.pdf) says existing homeowners' rate would not change but does not say who votes. The Travis County order and notice of election (https://votetravis.gov/wp-content/uploads/Travis-County-Order-of-Election.pdf, https://votetravis.gov/wp-content/uploads/G26-Travis-County-Notice-of-Election.pdf) do not list ballot styles or precincts. Sample ballots were 'coming soon' on votetravis.gov, and the ESD 4 voter-education page (https://www.esd4.org/voter-education-re-district-expansion) was blocked (permission request unanswered). Practical risk: if Travis County reports c205 as one combined total, that total cannot show whether both majorities were met.
